svg.title: Channel Partner Private Offer Readiness
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-cppo-readiness-gates; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Channel Partner Private Offer Readiness; subtitle: Four gates before an AWS CPPO goes to the buyer; caption: AWS walks resellers through listing eligibility, resale authorization, buyer targeting and cash forecasting before a CPPO is sent.; assumptions note: Gate order mirrors the Chapter Q5 operator gates. Payment timing uses only the 25-day average lag and the 7th-10th disbursement window reported by AWS.; note: Sources: Amazon Web Services [PkznZxwv3eg @ 00:01:43, 00:08:13, 00:12:57]; Amazon Web Services [pOUxsKDRzvM @ 00:02:26]; Amazon Web Services [vKzo7FINzss @ 00:02:42].; nodes: gate: G1; question: Does the ISV have a paid listing, and are you a registered AWS Marketplace seller?; pass next: G2; fail action: Do not quote; BYOL and free products are excluded from CPPO.; gate: G2; question: Have you accepted the seller's reseller agreement, and is the resale authorization inside its validity window?; pass next: G3; fail action: Hold the offer build; push the ISV for a recurring authorization instead of a one-time discount.; gate: G3; question: Will the buyer receive both the private offer link and the targeted AWS account ID?; pass next: G4; fail action: Put the account ID next to the link in the offer email; the buyer must be logged into that exact account.; gate: G4; question: Does the forecast pad for the 25-day average payment lag and any net 30, 45 or 60 terms?; pass next: Send the offer; cash lands between the 7th and 10th of the month after invoicing.; fail action: Pad the revenue forecast before committing numbers.

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Does the ISV have a paid listing, and are you a registered AWS Marketplace seller?; pass next: G2; fail action: Do not quote; BYOL and free products are excluded from CPPO.

gate: G2; question: Have you accepted the seller's reseller agreement, and is the resale authorization inside its validity window?; pass next: G3; fail action: Hold the offer build; push the ISV for a recurring authorization instead of a one-time discount.

gate: G3; question: Will the buyer receive both the private offer link and the targeted AWS account ID?; pass next: G4; fail action: Put the account ID next to the link in the offer email; the buyer must be logged into that exact account.

gate: G4; question: Does the forecast pad for the 25-day average payment lag and any net 30, 45 or 60 terms?; pass next: Send the offer; cash lands between the 7th and 10th of the month after invoicing.; fail action: Pad the revenue forecast before committing numbers.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order mirrors the Chapter Q5 operator gates. Payment timing uses only the 25-day average lag and the 7th-10th disbursement window reported by AWS.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order mirrors the Chapter Q5 operator gates. Payment timing uses only the 25-day average lag and the 7th-10th
